**Finding submitted: deviation (INDEMN).**

**What the document has.** Article XIV contains reciprocal indemnities. RevMed's indemnity (14.1) covers (a) its negligence/recklessness/willful misconduct, (b) material breach of its reps and warranties, and (c) material breach of its obligations — which, via covenant 13.4(b), picks up breach of Applicable Law. Section 14.3 supplies a full standard procedure (notice, control of defence, right to participate, settlement consent, cooperation, expense reimbursement), and 14.5 carves indemnity out of the consequential-damages exclusion with no monetary cap — both favourable to us, so no super-cap is needed.

**Why it still fails the fallback.** The fallback's material term is a vendor IP indemnity, and there is none:
- Third-party IP claims reach RevMed only indirectly, as a breach of the 13.2 reps; the patent non-infringement rep (13.2(f)) is knowledge-qualified and confined to the Development Candidate as at the Execution Date.
- Section 13.5 expressly disclaims any non-infringement warranty, and 10.7 puts the first burden of negotiating a third-party licence on us.
- Our own indemnity at 14.2(a) affirmatively covers claims arising from our Research, Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of Products — so freedom-to-operate exposure on the technology RevMed licensed to us lands on Sanofi.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** Smallest edit to reach the preferred position: a new limb 14.1(d) covering claims that the RevMed Licensed Technology (or activities conducted in accordance with the Agreement) infringes or misappropriates third-party IP, with the customary modification and combination exclusions, plus a conforming change of "(a) through (c)" to "(a) through (d)" in the 14.1 carve-out. The existing comparative-fault carve-outs in p0585 continue to apply, and we left RevMed's 14.2 protections untouched.
